precepts.text: Ahithophel's counsel to defile David's concubines, and how his counsel was esteemed as the oracle of God with both David and Absalom.
precepts.point: Now he asks Absalom to let him choose out twelve thousand men to pursue David that same night while David was weary and weak handed, to smite the king only and bring back all the people. He wanted the victory and the bragging rights of being the one who killed King David.

note.label: 2 Samuel 17: The Counsel of the Lord Shall Stand

precepts.why:
Absalom said to Ahithophel, “Give counsel among you what we shall do.” Ahithophel answered, “Go in unto thy father’s concubines, which he hath left to keep the house; and all Israel shall hear that thou art abhorred of thy father: then shall the hands of all that are with thee be strong.” That was already wicked counsel, before he ever asked for twelve thousand men.

Ahithophel was David’s own counselor turned traitor, being the devil the Bible speaks of, working deceit and betrayal from inside the gates of Israel. And “the counsel of Ahithophel, which he counselled in those days, was as if a man had enquired at the oracle of God: so was all the counsel of Ahithophel both with David and with Absalom.” That tells you he was very influential and had the gift of gab, so persuasive that his advice sounded almost biblical.

So when he said, “Let me now choose out twelve thousand men, and I will arise and pursue after David this night”, to come upon him “while he is weary and weak handed” and “smite the king only”, Absalom was hearing it from the man everyone listened to. He wanted the victory and the bragging rights of being the one who killed King David.

precepts.text: The Most High's own people rise up as an enemy; the enemies Christ said to forgive are the enemies of our people.
precepts.point: Now he asks Absalom to let him choose out twelve thousand men to pursue David that same night while David was weary and weak handed, to smite the king only and bring back all the people. He wanted the victory and the bragging rights of being the one who killed King David.

note.label: 2 Samuel 17: The Counsel of the Lord Shall Stand

precepts.why:
“Even of late my people is risen up as an enemy: ye pull off the robe with the garment from them that pass by securely as men averse from war.”

The Most High’s own people rise up as an enemy. Ahithophel was David’s own counselor, working betrayal from inside the gates of Israel, and here he asks to pursue David that same night and smite the king only.

The enemies Christ said to forgive are the enemies of our people.

precepts.text: David sends Hushai back to Absalom to defeat Ahithophel's counsel and to report through Zadok and Abiathar; the name Hushai means loyal to the king.
precepts.point: Absalom and all the men of Israel said Hushai's counsel was better than Ahithophel's. The Lord had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that He might bring evil upon Absalom. The Lord was working with Hushai and David, while Satan was in the spirit of Absalom and Ahithophel.

note.label: 2 Samuel 17: The Counsel of the Lord Shall Stand

precepts.why:
When David came to the top of the mount, Hushai the Archite met him “with his coat rent, and earth upon his head”. David sent him back: “if thou return to the city, and say unto Absalom, I will be thy servant, O king; as I have been thy father’s servant hitherto, so will I now also be thy servant: then mayest thou for me defeat the counsel of Ahithophel.” Whatever he heard out of the king’s house he was to tell Zadok and Abiathar the priests, and send to David by their sons Ahimaaz and Jonathan. The name Hushai means loyal to the king.

That is the man Absalom called when he wanted a second opinion: “Call now Hushai the Archite also, and let us hear likewise what he saith.” Hushai was a counterintelligence agent, a spy planted in righteousness, always siding with King David.

So he told Absalom, “The counsel that Ahithophel hath given is not good at this time.” He reminded him that his father and his men were mighty men, “chafed in their minds, as a bear robbed of her whelps in the field”, war ready and strategic, and that David “will not lodge with the people” but moves by night. He warned that if some were overthrown at the first, even he “whose heart is as the heart of a lion, shall utterly melt”, for all Israel knew David was a mighty man. David and his mighty men were on another level; none of Absalom’s thousands could compare to them.

Then he counselled that all Israel be gathered “from Dan even to Beer–sheba, as the sand that is by the sea for multitude”, with Absalom going to battle in his own person. It was deliberately inaccurate counsel that would waste time gathering troops and give David room to escape. Hushai did exactly what David sent him back to do: he defeated the counsel of Ahithophel.

precepts.text: Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel at the gate, promising he would do them justice if he were made judge.
precepts.point: Absalom and all the men of Israel said Hushai's counsel was better than Ahithophel's. The Lord had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that He might bring evil upon Absalom. The Lord was working with Hushai and David, while Satan was in the spirit of Absalom and Ahithophel.

note.label: 2 Samuel 17: The Counsel of the Lord Shall Stand

precepts.why:
Absalom “prepared him chariots and horses, and fifty men to run before him”, stood beside the way of the gate, and told every man who came to the king for judgment, “See, thy matters are good and right; but there is no man deputed of the king to hear thee.” Then he said, “Oh that I were made judge in the land, that every man which hath any suit or cause might come unto me, and I would do him justice!” So he stole the hearts of the men of Israel at the gate.

That is how Absalom came to be sitting with Ahithophel and Hushai, asking how to take his father. He took the seat himself. But the Lord was not with him: the Lord was working with Hushai and David, while Satan was in the spirit of Absalom and Ahithophel.

precepts.text: God set the members every one in the body as it pleased Him; promotion comes from the Most High, not from a man taking the seat himself.
precepts.point: Absalom and all the men of Israel said Hushai's counsel was better than Ahithophel's. The Lord had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that He might bring evil upon Absalom. The Lord was working with Hushai and David, while Satan was in the spirit of Absalom and Ahithophel.

note.label: 2 Samuel 17: The Counsel of the Lord Shall Stand

precepts.why:
“But now hath God set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him.” Promotion comes from the Most High, not from a man taking the seat himself.

Absalom tried to take the seat, stealing the hearts of Israel at the gate and rising up against his own father. But God sets the members in the body as it pleases him, and he had not set Absalom on that throne. That is why the counsel that would have won it for him was defeated, and evil came upon Absalom instead.

precepts.text: There are many devices in a man's heart, but the counsel of the Lord, that shall stand.
precepts.point: Absalom and all the men of Israel said Hushai's counsel was better than Ahithophel's. The Lord had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that He might bring evil upon Absalom. The Lord was working with Hushai and David, while Satan was in the spirit of Absalom and Ahithophel.

note.label: 2 Samuel 17: The Counsel of the Lord Shall Stand

precepts.why:
“There are many devices in a man’s heart; nevertheless the counsel of the Lord, that shall stand.”

Ahithophel had his device and Hushai had his. “And Absalom and all the men of Israel said, The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel.” But it was not Absalom’s choosing that decided it: “For the Lord had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that the Lord might bring evil upon Absalom.” The counsel of the Lord stood.

There is safety in a multitude of counselors, but only where the counsel is according to thus saith the Lord. A counselor who does not go to the scriptures is not one you should want.

precepts.text: A Psalm of David when he fled from Absalom his son; the Lord is a shield for him, sustaining him in sleep though ten thousands set themselves against him.
precepts.point: The two came up out of the well and told David to arise and pass quickly over the water. David and all the people passed over Jordan by the morning light, and there lacked not one of them that was not gone over.

note.label: 2 Samuel 17: The Counsel of the Lord Shall Stand

precepts.why:
This is a Psalm of David when he fled from Absalom his son: “Lord, how are they increased that trouble me! many are they that rise up against me. Many there be which say of my soul, There is no help for him in God.” But “thou, O Lord, art a shield for me; my glory, and the lifter up of mine head.”

That is this night. Hushai sent word by Zadok and Abiathar: “Lodge not this night in the plains of the wilderness, but speedily pass over; lest the king be swallowed up, and all the people that are with him.” Jonathan and Ahimaaz waited by En-rogel and a wench carried the word to them. A lad saw them and told Absalom, so they hid in a well in a man’s house in Bahurim, and a woman spread a covering over the well’s mouth and ground corn upon it to camouflage it. She told Absalom’s servants, “They be gone over the brook of water”, and the pursuers returned to Jerusalem.

The Most High put his spirit on certain people to orchestrate his plan. Often when a man tries to do evil to another, it falls back on him, for he that diggeth a pit shall fall therein.

“I laid me down and slept; I awaked; for the Lord sustained me. I will not be afraid of ten thousands of people, that have set themselves against me round about.” David arose and all the people with him passed over Jordan, and “by the morning light there lacked not one of them that was not gone over Jordan.” “Salvation belongeth unto the Lord: thy blessing is upon thy people.”

precepts.text: Evil pursueth sinners, but to the righteous good shall be repaid.
precepts.point: To be righteous is to observe to do all the commandments of the Lord; all unrighteousness is sin, and sin is the transgression of the law. David was righteous and did not want to war against his own son, yet good was repaid to him, while the sinner was pursued by his own evil.

note.label: 2 Samuel 17: The Counsel of the Lord Shall Stand

precepts.why:
“Evil pursueth sinners: but to the righteous good shall be repayed.”

When Ahithophel “saw that his counsel was not followed, he saddled his ass, and arose, and gat him home to his house, to his city, and put his household in order, and hanged himself, and died”. The evil counsel he devised reared its head around and bit its author. Evil pursued the sinner.

And to the righteous good was repaid. David did not want to war against his own son, yet good was repaid to him, while Ahithophel was pursued by his own evil.

precepts.text: It shall be our righteousness if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord.
precepts.point: To be righteous is to observe to do all the commandments of the Lord; all unrighteousness is sin, and sin is the transgression of the law. David was righteous and did not want to war against his own son, yet good was repaid to him, while the sinner was pursued by his own evil.

note.label: 2 Samuel 17: The Counsel of the Lord Shall Stand

precepts.why:
“And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.”

That is what it means to be righteous: to observe to do all the commandments of the Lord. So when the scripture says good shall be repaid to the righteous, this is who it means. David was righteous and good was repaid to him, while Ahithophel the sinner was pursued by his own evil until he hanged himself.

precepts.text: All unrighteousness is sin; to be unrighteous is to not keep the commandments.

“All unrighteousness is sin”. To be unrighteous is to not keep the commandments, and sin is the transgression of the law.
